articles.title: Baylor, DJ Lagway fall just short of comeback vs. Auburn as risky 2-point attempt fails in closing seconds
articles.summary: It looked like Lagway had a running lane, but the QB was dealing with a bum ankle from an earlier hit.
articles.body:
Baylor lost to Auburn in a nail-biter on Saturday after the Bears were stopped just short of the goal line on a potential winning 2-point try in the final seconds.

The Tigers were up for most of the game, but the Bears hung around. New Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway threw a touchdown pass with 9 seconds left to cut Auburn's lead to 17-16. That wound up being the final score in Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Bears head coach Dave Aranda chose to roll the dice and keep the offense on the field, hoping the momentum from the scoring drive could help them get into the end zone.

Lagway took the snap and rolled right. He tried to hit tight end Matthew Klopfenstein.

The throw was a little behind Klopfenstein, but he turned back and caught it. He tried to get the ball into the end zone, but was stuffed at the line by Auburn safety Eric Winters.

The risk did not pay off for the Bears as they dropped to 0-1 in the year.

The dual-threat Lagway took a hit early in the game, and he was favoring his leg down the stretch. This forced him to remain in the pocket, taking away a typically big part of his game.

Lagway finished the game 27-of-54 passing for 333 yards with two touchdowns, an interception, and a lost fumble. The quarterback's fourth-quarter drive ended as he found Gavin Freeman for the 5-yard score.

Auburn gets its first win under new head coach Alex Golesh, who came over from South Florida after Auburn fired Hugh Freeze amid a 5-7 season.

Lagway is in his first season with Baylor. He began his career as a five-star recruit at Florida. Last season, he played in 12 games for the Gators, but struggled mightily. Lagway threw for 2,264 yards with 16 touchdowns and 14 interceptions.

The Bears finished last year with a 5-7 record. Former quarterback Sawyer Robertson went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, but his absence led Aranda to bring in Lagway.

Baylor will look to build on the fact that they kept the game close and scored on the last-second drive. The Bears should have a lower-profile matchup next week to bounce back as Baylor welcomes Prairie View A&M to Waco.

articles.title: JAX Armada supporters ask MLS Pro league about status of team, chances of beginning play in 2027
articles.summary: A group supporting the Jacksonville Armada soccer team is asking the pro league it plans to join if a proposed ownership change is going to be approved to ke...
articles.body:
A group supporting the Jacksonville Armada soccer team is asking the pro league it plans to join if a proposed ownership change is going to be approved to keep a 2027 launch on track.

The Bold City Ultras wrote to the MLS NEXT Pro league - a bridge between elite youth academies and Major League Soccer (MLS) - when it plans to rule on a pending ownership change of the Armada from Robert Palmer to an investor group led by Chris Campione.

"The sale was announced publicly on October 30, 2025," a letter by Bold City Ultras emailed to Action News Jax read. "Ten months later, the approval has not been issued."

The supporters group says the ownership change approval by the league is needed because new owners have said they would suspend operations September 4 absent a decision.

The uncertainty also clouds a decision by the city of Jacksonville on an historic Eastside parcel planned for a new stadium for the soccer team, it said. The group's letter said a decision on the parcel is needed by September 10.

The Armada remain listed on the MLS NEXT Pro website as an "additional MLS-affiliated and independent club" that will join the league "in the years ahead."

articles.title: Dan Lanning Says Oregon Has 'A Lot to Fix' After Narrowly Avoiding Boise State's Upset Bid
articles.summary: No. 2 Oregon football escaped visiting Boise State's upset effort by defeating the Broncos 34-27 on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
No. 2 Oregon football escaped visiting Boise State's upset effort by defeating the Broncos 34-27 on Saturday afternoon.

Afterward, Oregon head coach Dan Lanning said during his postgame interview with CBS Sports' Jenny Dell that the Ducks have "a lot to fix" and "a lot to clean up."

Oregon was a 24.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but Boise State kicker Canaan More tied the game at 27 following his 36-yard field goal with 8:45 left in regulation.

However, Ducks quarterback Dante Moore responded with a 62-yard touchdown pass to Dakorien Moore just two plays from scrimmage later.

Boise State had two more possessions but never threatened to score after going three-and-out and then turning the ball over on downs at its own 31-yard line.

articles.title: Tennessee Dolly Parton tributes: Vols stage massive stadium singalongs to honor music legend
articles.summary: The Vols found an appropriate way to honor the late Dolly Parton.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton and the state of Tennessee go hand in hand. While the country star lived and worked near Nashville, the state's flagship university in Knoxville is honoring her in its season opener in more ways than one.

As the Volunteers started the season against Furman, their fans paid tribute to Parton with a massive singalong as the singer's hits played for a crowd of more than 100,000.

Tennessee also honored Parton as part of its uniform, something the Volunteers plan to do for the entire season.

Here's a look at the singalong of all singalongs in Knoxville.

More than 102,000 Tennessee fans sang Parton's "I Will Always Love You" during the Volunteers' game against Furman, a 56-9 win.

The Vols then changed up their fourth-quarter song and played Parton's "My Tennessee Mountain Home" to pay tribute to the singer, who died on Aug. 25.

Tennessee previously announced it would honor Parton with a special helmet sticker throughout the season:

Here's more to know about Parton's connection to Tennessee.

What was Dolly Parton's connection to Tennessee?

Parton didn't attend the University of Tennessee or go to college at all, but she was born and raised in the state. With Tennessee being the state's flagship university, the school developed a bond with the singer.

Parton received an honorary doctorate from Tennessee in 2009, and she memorably sang "Rocky Top" at Neyland Stadium after being escorted onto the field by Peyton Manning during a game against Georgia in 2023.

Parton died of cancer in Nashville on Aug. 25. Parton had been open about battling health issues in the years leading up to her death, but she never disclosed that she was dealing with cancer.

The singer, who was 80, worked "up until the day she died," her manager told Billboard .

On Tuesday, he could make his 100th competitive appearance for the Black & Yellow. 99 games in, he has an incredible 62 goals to his name, trailing only Erling Haaland and Lothar Emmerich.

Haaland scored a staggering total of 86 goals in 89 competitive matches for BVB. Emmerich found the net 64 times in his first 100 Bundesliga matches for Borussia Dortmund.

articles.title: Texas football, Will Muschamp's defense draw raves in Texas State blowout | Golden
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns took care of business in the opener and showed there are other levels they can reach entering the upcoming showdown against Ohio State.
articles.body:
First review from the press box on the 2026 Texas Longhorns ?

Steve Sarkisian will take an opener like this all day long. Texas played up to its ranking at times and if we can say that this time next week, the Horns will be on to something.

The good news is the No. 5 Horns have plenty of room for improvement after the 59-7 blowout of the neighboring Texas State Bobcats .

Quarterback Arch Manning looked miles better than the kid who struggled in his first real at Ohio State in 2025. He completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns. He looked in command of the position and did a commendable job of spreading the ball around to his bevy of weapons, including veteran wideout Ryan Wingo who caught seven passes for 121 yards and a score. Manning did stub his biggest foot by throwing into double coverage for an interception at the end of the first half but that was the only blip.

In true Arch fashion, he bounced back with a deep throw to Wingo to open the third quarter followed by a 20-yard TD pass to high-priced import Cam Coleman while taking a wicked shot to the head. Overall, he did nothing to dim the spotlight that will be on him on and Ohio State starter Julian Sayin for that delicious top-five matchup at DKR next week

The run game wasn't a world beater but serviceable at 4.4 yards per carry. That said, newcomer Hollywood Smothers is an absolute terror in the passing game. He grabbed three aerials for 28 yards and a touchdown. I could see him catching upwards of 60 passes out of the backfield this fall. The Horns haven't had this versatile of a back since 2024 when Jaydon Blue caught 42 passes for 368 yards and six touchdowns.

What about Will Muschamp and that newfangled defense? It was what Dr. Sarkisian ordered. Any time you can hold a team that ranked fifth nationally to a single touchdown and over 150 yards under last season's total, it's a win. Game balls go out Alex January, who batted down a fourth-down pass in the early going, Graceson Littleton , who put a charge into the sellout crowd with a 60-yard fumble return for a touchdown and dynamic duo Colin Simmons and Rasheem Biles , who came up with a fumble recovery and interception, respectively. Biles' strip also set up Littleton's scoop and score.

New kicker Gianni Spetik tacked on a 48-yard field goal for a nice debut.

Now America can turn its attention to the renewal of a hot nonconference rivalry, that is, if we're counting Texas' wins over Ohio State in the 2005 and 2008 seasons. The Buckeyes have had the better of it lately. They kept the Longhorns out of the national championship game in 2024 then handed them a 14-7 loss in last season's opener.

In case you're wondering, the last time the two met in Austin, the top-ranked Buckeyes routed No. 2 Texas 24-7 back in 2006 in young quarterback Colt McCoy 's first big test as the starter in place in Vince Young.

The Horns are searching for some new memories.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 1
articles.summary: Although the official return of college football has passed, Week 1 marked the first full Saturday of the 2026 season. More than a hundred FBS teams returned to the field and kicked off their campaign.
articles.body:
Although the official return of college football has passed, Week 1 marked the first full Saturday of the 2026 season. More than a hundred FBS teams returned to the field and kicked off their campaign.

Once again, and finally, we have a complete slate to dissect.

From an implosion by Rutgers on Thursday to Miami's sharp opener on Friday to Oregon's escape on Saturday, it's already been a busy weekend.

The main event is still looming on Saturday night as a prime-time showdown between Clemson and LSU doubles as Lane Kiffin's debut in Baton Rouge.

This piece will be updated throughout Labor Day weekend.

Emphasis on result . Because that, my friends, was ugly.

Julian Lewis completed just 14-of-27 passes for 124 yards—an unimpressive 4.6 yards per attempt. There were too many punts, a missed field goal and Georgia Tech returned a kickoff for a touchdown.

It was an ugly evening for Colorado. Simultaneously, in this result-oriented world, CU landed the only thing that matters: a win.

As time expired, Boo Carter blocked GT's decisive 45-yard kick. Colorado players rushed onto the field and celebrated a 14-13 victory.

After the Buffs plummeted to 3-9 (with a 1-8 mark in Big 12 action) last season, Deion Sanders entered 2026 needing a resurgent year. His seat isn't necessarily hot , but another rough campaign would create an unpleasant conversation in Boulder. That still may happen. It's a long season.

Colorado still won, though. And in Week 1, you don't complain about ugly wins.

It's certainly possible to have a worse opening game, given that a team theoretically could lose 70-0 or something like that.

But, my word, Rutgers just endured a nightmare.

The offense ripped down the field for a touchdown on the first possession of the game. It seemed like everything was going as planned. And then, Massachusetts—which finished 0-12 last year and hadn't defeated an FBS opponent since 2023—proceeded to score 30 straight points.

Rutgers is not a powerhouse program. We know that. But UMass? Putting up nearly 400 yards with four takeaways in a 37-21 thumping on the road?

That was a shocking, inexcusable, disastrous showing from Rutgers.

In a 45-6 rout of Stanford, Miami did exactly what a heavy favorite is supposed to do. Most importantly, so did the superstars.

Malachi Toney reeled in 12 passes for a program-record 234 yards, catching three touchdowns from new quarterback Darian Mensah. The transfer from Duke completed 27-of-30 throws for 401 yards and five scores in his Miami debut.

It's fair to say Heisman Trophy voters are on high alert.

Toney, who flashed the iconic pose after his TDs, was simply untouchable. He shredded anyone Stanford threw at him in man coverage. Mensah also hit Cooper Barkate—who transferred with him from Duke—and Daylyn Upshaw for touchdowns to round out an outstanding game.

Miami has issues to address in run blocking, an injury worry with key cornerback OJ Frederique Jr. and a depth concern at linebacker. Don't crown the 'Canes yet.

But this combination of Mensah and Toney already looks special.

As expected, the conclusion was never in jeopardy. Alabama rolled to a 48-10 victory over an outmatched East Carolina team.

The spotlight was always going to focus on Keelon Russell.

Making his first career start, the redshirt freshman—a 5-star prospect in the 2025 class—backed up his lofty billing. He went 18-of-30 for 256 yards, adding a team-leading 86 yards on the ground with a touchdown.

Russell had a couple of nervy throws, and he invited too many hits while running. He'll undoubtedly be coached to slide or head toward the sideline more often.

Nevertheless, he flashed a terrific mix of decision-making, arm talent and elusiveness. There's no question the best version of Russell can propel Bama to the College Football Playoff this season.

Baylor is facing some pressure because head coach Dave Aranda is sitting on a reasonably hot seat. Auburn, meanwhile, has posted five straight seven-loss records and is desperate to improve under new boss Alex Golesh.

Saturday's clash did not exactly fire up either fan base.

Inside the home of the NFL's Atlanta Falcons, both offenses struggled. Auburn QB Byrum Brown tossed three interceptions, while Baylor counterpart DJ Lagway threw a pick and lost a fumble. Neither side had an effective rushing attack, and both units had a turnover on downs— plus a missed field goal, for good measure.

Thanks to a fantastic hit by safety Eric Winters to prevent a two-point conversion, Auburn stole a dramatic 17-16 victory. As with Colorado, every win is a good win. That should never be taken for granted.

Looking ahead, though, Auburn and Baylor have a ton to prove.

On one hand, Boise State is a quality team. It's not like a lower-division program stuck with Oregon in a truly stunning game.

For those who believe Oregon is a prime championship threat, however, this was not a convincing home opener. Dan Lanning's squad fell behind 17-7 and needed a couple of late defensive stops to outlast Boise 34-27.

Leaping off the bandwagon is unnecessary. That'd be a rash decision, especially as the program breaks in new coordinators on both sides of the ball.

Simultaneously, the Ducks had a flurry of head-scratching mistakes—the kinds that an elite contender will not make—with 10 penalties chief among them.

Oregon's talent is undeniable. Its execution will be monitored closely.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns transfers worth every penny, and other UT vs Texas State observations
articles.summary: Arch Manning looked great, the defense looked great, the newcomers looked great. In fact, just about everything went Texas' way in Saturday's 59-7 win over T...
articles.body:
What did Texas football get out of Saturday's 59-7 win over Texas State , a not-too-competitive season opener at Royal-Memorial Stadium that came down either to the Bobcats being literally out of their league or the Longhorns ready to take the country by storm. (More on that next week, though.)

Actually, the No. 5 Longhorns got quite a lot out of Saturday:

• Arch Manning was efficient and productive, threw for 305 yards and four touchdowns, completed 74% of his passes and led Texas to touchdowns on six of his seven drives on the day. He gave way to KJ Lacey (6 of 7 for 55 yards) in the third quarter. Manning looked good on deep balls, too.

• The Horns got some big plays from both of their new running backs, including a 45-yard run and a receiving TD by Hollywood Smothers and 13- and 21-yard TD runs from Raleek Brown .

• Texas' drives went TD, TD, TD, INT, TD, TD, TD, FG and TD on the day. The Horns scored on a defensive TD in there, too.

• And there were no significant injuries and Texas should head into next week's home showdown with No. 1 Ohio State with some confidence.

Here are some observations we saw from Saturday's win:

The way Manning played Saturday won't dull the Heisman hype that has followed the Texas quarterback since, well, he stepped on campus. Sure, he threw an ill-advised pick into the end zone that cost the Longhorns points at the end of the first half. But the numbers will jump out to Heisman voters: 305 yards, 20-of-27 passing and four touchdowns.

But you know what will leap out even further? A win over Ohio State.

Yes, new wideout Cam Coleman scored the first touchdown of the season for Texas and ended the game with a respectable 70 yards and a pair of scores on three catches. But returning starter Ryan Wingo keyed the passing game with seven catches for 121 yards and a touchdown. No one on the roster has as much experience playing catch with Manning than Wingo, and the third-year receiver proved the quarterback's go-to target.

New LB Rasheem Biles shows why he drew a big paycheck

Maybe we'll never know what Texas paid Rasheem Biles to transfer from Pittsburgh to Texas in the offseason. But the senior earned every penny against the Bobcats, however many there are. He forced a fumble that slot corner Graceson Littleton returned for a 59-yard touchdown, and he picked off Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson in the second half. He looks like the linchpin for new defensive coordinator Will Muschamp.

(1) Texas' first TD of the season was Coleman's 6-yard catch off a Manning toss into the corner of the end zone. Coleman follows these five former Longhorns as the first to score a TD in Sarkisian's first six years: RB Bijan Robinson 's 18-yard catch in 2021, RB Keilan Robinson 's blocked punt return in 2022, RB Jonathon Brooks ' 37-yard catch in 2023, RB Quintrevion Wisner 's 3-yard run in 2024 and WR Parker Livingstone 's 32-yard catch last year. (2) Gameballs go to Wingo and Biles. Nods to DT Alex January's tipped fourth-down pass, Littleton's big defensive TD, K Gianni Spetic's 48-yard FG and WR Sterling Berkhalter, who had the catch of the game. (3) Looking for nits? Manning's end zone interception, freshman RB Derrek Cooper ended the game in a walking boot, and ... punter Mac Chiumento will head into next week's big game with no kicks under his belt, maybe?

6:30 p.m. next Saturday at DKR. It's an ABC game.

The national game of the year, for sure in Week 2 but arguably also of the whole regular season, pits the No. 1 Buckeyes and the No. 5 Longhorns in Austin, where Texas is 19-1 in its last 20 home games, including a 5-1 record vs. ranked teams. Ohio State, which has registered a 2024 CFP win and a 2025 regular-season win over the Horns in recent years, will be favored.

This is how our own Cedric Golden called it in August: "This is the one Texas (has) to have. The Horns jump to No. 1 in the country, but much work remains. Texas 24, Ohio State 20 ."

articles.title: Florida Revives 'Gator Bait' Cheer 6 Years After It Was Banned Because of 'Racist Imagery'
articles.summary: GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — The University of Florida revived its "gator bait" cheer Saturday night during its season opener, bringing it back more than six years after the school banned it because of "horrific historic racist imagery" associated with the phrase.
articles.body:
GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — The University of Florida revived its "gator bait" cheer Saturday night during its season opener, bringing it back more than six years after the school banned it because of "horrific historic racist imagery" associated with the phrase.

New school president Stuart Bell said in June that "traditions matter" and hinted that the cheer could return because "it's meaningful to the Gator family."

It returned to the Swamp early in the first quarter against Florida Atlantic — and was welcomed with a raucous reception. It was far from a surprise because clips of Florida's band practicing the accompanying tune were shared on social media this week.

Former Florida president Kent Fuchs announced in June 2020 that Florida's band would no longer play the musical cue prompting fans to chant "gator bait" because of concerns about possible racial undertones. Art depicting alligator hunters using Black babies to lure the animals into the open was popular in the late 1800s and early 1900s.

The decision came amid a broader national reckoning on race following the murder of George Floyd while in police custody in Minneapolis in May 2020.

Many Florida fans met Fuchs' decree with disdain, arguing the cheer was a tradition and never performed with any racist intentions.

Bell seemed to agree. He was Florida's sole finalist as president after the school began its third search in four years in December 2025. Florida's Board of Governors rejected the selection of Dr. Santa Ono, the former president of the University of Michigan, in June 2025.

Bell took over a school that eliminated all diversity, equity and inclusion positions in 2024 after a new state rule that prohibited the addition of such programs.

Florida closed the Office of the Chief Diversity Officer and stopped DEI-focused contracts with external vendors. The $5 million in annual funds previously allocated for UF's DEI initiatives, including salaries and expenditures, was placed into a faculty recruitment fund.

articles.title: College football Week 1 winners and losers: The year of the quarterback has gotten off to a stellar start
articles.summary: Yes, a lot of top teams played inferior opponents in Week 1. But the stat lines that star QBs put up in those games were still eye-opening.
articles.body:
College football's year of the star quarterback got off to a roaring start.

Sure, this year's Week 1 slate wasn't exactly the strongest we've ever seen. Just one game over college football's opening weekend featured two teams ranked in the preseason AP Top 25. And it hasn't even kicked off yet. No. 9 Ole Miss plays No. 24 Louisville on Sunday.

Teams like Ohio State, Texas, and Georgia all covered massive spreads against inferior opponents. But they did that, in part, because of the stat lines their star quarterbacks put up. Just look at the performances by the quarterbacks among the nation's top teams this week.

Even though receivers like Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith and Miami's Malachi Toney had incredible games in Week 1, they have a lot of work to do to be favorites for the Heisman Trophy because of the quarterback depth at the top of college football.

Sayin had as many incompletions as he had total touchdowns in the Buckeyes' 56-3 win over Ball State . Sayin was 21-of-25 passing for 320 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing for his first career score on the ground. Don't expect Sayin's run game to be a prominent feature of the Ohio State offense all season long, but he at least won't go his entire Buckeye career without a rushing TD.

The Ducks had to sweat way more than they expected in a 34-27 win over Boise State . But the Broncos are a potential playoff team. Moore was 28-of-37 for 378 yards and three touchdowns and didn't commit a turnover. After a slow start, Moore found tight end Jamari Johnson on a fantastic throw down the middle of the field to end the first half.

The Bulldogs put Tennessee State away in the first quarter of a 63-3 win . Georgia had 28 first-quarter points on an extremely hot day in Athens and Stockton had just one incompletion before he got to watch the rest of the game from the sideline. He was 15-of-16 passing for 202 yards and three touchdowns.

Yes, Manning threw a bad interception into triple coverage in the end zone late in the second quarter. But that was the only blemish on an otherwise stellar day in Texas' 59-7 victory over Texas State. Manning was 20-of-27 passing for 305 yards and threw four TDs. Two of those scores went to Auburn transfer Cam Coleman in his first game at Texas.

By the way, Sayin and Manning meet in Week 2.

Hoover immediately endeared himself to Indiana fans when he threw a touchdown pass to Charlie Becker in the second quarter with blood streaming down his face. Hoover suffered a cut to the top of his nose on a facemask penalty just a few plays before, but didn't exit the game until he found Becker for a 21-3 lead. Indiana beat North Texas 52-16 as Hoover was 13 of 16 for 231 yards and four touchdowns.

The Trojans became the first team to go 2-0 in 2026 with a 39-0 win over Fresno State on Friday night . Maiava was 23-of-25 passing for 349 yards and three touchdowns in the win and has as many incompletions as he does total touchdowns across USC's two wins. Maiava has thrown for 635 yards and five touchdowns and has also rushed for a score.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

UMass: Thursday night was the biggest win for the Minutemen since the 1998 FCS national title. No, that's not hyperbolic, either. UMass was a 29.5-point underdog to Rutgers and dominated the Scarlet Knights in a 37-21 win. It was the first win over a power conference opponent in UMass history as Virginia Tech transfer Pop Watson had as many touchdowns as incompletions. Watson threw three scores and was 19-of-22 passing for 197 yards. UMass also rushed for 200 yards and held Rutgers to just 30 on the ground thanks to sacks and forced four turnovers of Rutgers QB Dylan Lonergan.

Tulsa: Could the Golden Hurricane break a four-year bowl drought in 2026? A year after beating Oklahoma State in a game that led to Mike Gundy's firing, Tulsa beat the Cowboys again in a 24-10 win. It was the first game for new OSU coach Eric Morris after he arrived from North Texas.

Morris' Mean Green was one of the best teams in the American Conference in 2025. And he brought a bunch of his players with him to Stillwater, including QB Drew Mestemaker, RB Caleb Hawkins and WR Wyatt Young. Saturday, a team with some of the best players in the American in 2025 couldn't beat a team that won just one conference game a season ago. With games against Sam Houston and East Texas A&M coming up, Tulsa has a great shot to be 3-0 before going to Arkansas in Week 4.

Tennessee QB Faizon Brandon: The 18-year-old's first collegiate start could hardly have gone better. Brandon threw for three touchdowns and rushed for two more in No. 20 Tennessee's 56-9 win over Furman . Brandon became the first SEC quarterback to throw for three scores and add two others on the ground in his first start since Cam Newton in 2010. Newton went on to win the Heisman Trophy.

We're not making a Heisman prediction just yet for the true freshman. But it was obvious why he was the winner of Tennessee's QB competition in camp, even if Saturday's game was against an FCS opponent.

Army and Navy: Both teams played FCS opponents on Saturday. Both teams ran over, around and through those FCS opponents.

Army rushed 57 times for 569 yards and eight touchdowns in its 59-3 win over Bryant. Sixteen different players had at least one carry and only Zach Mundell — who rushed four times for 105 yards — topped 87 yards. It's fair to say that was a team effort.

Navy had 73 carries for 506 yards in its 42-15 victory over Towson. QB Braxton Woodson did most of that damage as he had 23 carries for 200 yards and three touchdowns. Fourteen different Midshipmen ran the ball at least once.

Boise State: It's hard to make this category after a loss. But the Broncos made it clear why they are a favorite to make the College Football Playoff after their 34-27 defeat to No. 2 Oregon. Two years ago, Boise State lost to the Ducks on a last second field goal before winning the Mountain West and easily making the playoff as the top non-power conference team. With the American Conference looking wide-open and the Pac-12 boasting seven other solid programs, a conference title and an 11-2 season should be enough for Boise State to be in the postseason field once again after how Saturday's game played out.

Virginia Tech: In 2025, Hokies running backs accounted for a grand total of three rushing touchdowns all season. Yes, you read that correctly. Just three.

Well, that number has already been eclipsed in 2026. Jefrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. combined for four rushing touchdowns in the first half against VMI on Saturday night. In fact, Overton's second score of the game with 4:56 to go in the first quarter tied last year's season total. Not a bad way to start the James Franklin era.

Rutgers: Where does the second Greg Schiano era go from here? The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach is in his seventh season in his Rutgers reboot. It hasn't been nearly as successful as his first stint. Of course, the Scarlet Knights were in the Big East and not the Big Ten back then, but Rutgers had eight or more wins in five of Schiano's final six seasons before taking the Bucs job in 2012.

Since he's been back, Rutgers hasn't won more than seven games in a single season and went 5-7 a year ago. And if you can't beat UMass at home, who are you going to beat in a Big Ten schedule that includes No. 14 USC, No. 6 Indiana, No. 16 Michigan, No. 18 Penn State and road trips to Maryland and Wisconsin? A loss at Boston College in Week 2 will be the sign of an extremely long season to come in Piscataway.

Georgia Tech: Better clock management would have given the Yellow Jackets a win over Colorado on Thursday night. Instead, Georgia Tech is 0-1 after a late TD by the Buffaloes and a blocked field goal as time expired resulted in a 14-13 Colorado win.

Leading 10-7, the Yellow Jackets got the ball with 7:35 remaining in the fourth quarter. Georgia Tech proceeded to run 12 offensive plays, but kicked a field goal from the Colorado 11-yard line with 1:40 to go for a six-point lead.

If Georgia Tech had snapped the ball later in the play clock over the course of that drive, Colorado could have had fewer than 20 seconds and no timeouts when it got the ball back for its game-winning drive.

Stanford: It's hard to cover a star wide receiver like Malachi Toney. And Stanford was a very good — or bad — example of that on Friday night. Toney had 12 catches for 234 yards and three scores in the Hurricanes' blowout win . And just look at how open he was on two of his TDs.

The 2026 season was always going to be a rebuilding year under first-year coach Tavita Pritchard. It's the former Stanford QB's first head-coaching job and he's inherited a program that had an interim coach in Frank Reich for the entirety of the 2025 season and hasn't won more than four games in a full season since 2018. Oh, there's a lot more travel involved now too as Stanford is a member of the ACC. Friday night showed that Stanford is still going to be among the bottom teams in the ACC for a little while longer.

Charlotte: Making Charlotte a competitive program might be a bigger task than Tim Albin expected. The 49ers lost 43-41 at home in triple overtime to The Citadel on Saturday.

Charlotte had 538 total yards, but quarterback Cole Gonzales threw two interceptions and The Citadel didn't turn the ball over at all. The Bulldogs' triple-option offense rushed for 268 yards on 50 carries for the program's first win over an FBS team since a 27-24 overtime win over Georgia Tech.

After moving to the American from Conference USA in 2023, Charlotte is 9-28 overall and just 1-12 in Albin's tenure.

articles.title: CFB Fans Stunned After Refs Put 1 Second on Clock for Bryce Underwood, Michigan Hail Mary vs. WMU
articles.summary: No. 16 Michigan narrowly survived an upset loss at the hands of Western Michigan on Saturday, securing a 13-12 win following a wild finish.
articles.body:
No. 16 Michigan narrowly survived an upset loss at the hands of Western Michigan on Saturday, securing a 13-12 win following a wild finish.

As Michigan trailed 12-7 with seven seconds left in the fourth quarter and the ball at Western Michigan's 47-yard line, Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt went out of bounds as time expired.

Watch: CFB QB's face bloodied after facemask penalty

However, officials determined that one second remained on the game clock. During Michigan's second Hail Mary try, Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan in the end zone to emerge victorious.

Fans and pundits were shocked by the finish.

NBC officiating analyst Terry McAulay suggested that the stadium clock used by officials during the replay review may have been different than the clock seen on the broadcast replay (via Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger ).

Despite narrowly pulling out a win, Michigan's overall performance was concerning.

The Wolverines routinely struggled to move the chains, as they only mustered 12 first downs while converting just three of 10 opportunities on third down. They also committed nine penalties for 80 yards.

Michigan found the end zone on its opening drive of the game to take an early 7-0 lead, but it wouldn't score again until the final play of the fourth quarter.

Underwood finished 12-of-22 for 170 yards and one touchdown compared to one interception. He also rushed for 47 yards and a score, but lost a fumble.

Michigan now sits at 1-0, although the team will look to make improvements moving forward.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Jokes About LSU Not Having NFL Players While Holding 31-3 Halftime Lead vs. Clemson

articles.body:
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin joked about the Tigers not having NFL players on their roster while taking a 31-3 halftime lead over Clemson on Saturday.

"Imagine if we had pro players," Kiffin told ESPN's Holly Rowe at the end of the first half.

LSU chose not to add tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris to its roster on Friday despite both players becoming eligible to return to college due to a Louisiana judge issuing a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in their eligibility case.

Wright was waived by the Cleveland Browns in training camp before committing to the Tigers, while Harris was waived by the New Orleans Saints.

While both were pursued by Kiffin and Co., neither was on the roster for Saturday's season opener.

articles.title: Western Michigan HC Lance Taylor Reacts to Michigan's Controversial Win on Bryce Underwood Hail Mary
articles.summary: Western Michigan head coach Lance Taylor reacted to the controversial Michigan Hail Mary on the final play of his team's 13-12 loss to the No. 16 Wolverines on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Western Michigan head coach Lance Taylor reacted to the controversial Michigan Hail Mary on the final play of his team's 13-12 loss to the No. 16 Wolverines on Saturday night.

"I have not seen the clip," Taylor told reporters after the game. "Several people have mentioned it to me that the game was over. One, our commissioner has already reached out. Normally he handles those type of situations and reviews. I thought that the crew tonight did a really nice job handling multiple close calls and review situations."

"I know when I looked up at the clock, it was past zeros before we touched it," he added. "I knew that they would review it, it was the last play of the game. Because we defended it so well, wasn't worried or concerned about our guys going out and defending it a second time. Unfortunately, we did not defend it as well the second time."

Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna and interim athletic director Elaine Russell also spoke on the situation:

Michigan trailed by five points and had the ball at Western Michigan's 47-yard line with seven seconds left in the fourth quarter. A Hail Mary attempt from Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood was unsuccessful as time ran out, although officials reviewed the play and put one second back on the clock.

Underwood's second Hail Mary attempt was caught by JJ Buchanan in the end zone, resulting in a win for Michigan.

While Taylor's squad couldn't emerge victorious, it was still a valiant effort overall.

The Broncos completely shut down a Michigan offense that averaged 396.9 yards and 27.5 points per game last season.

The Wolverines finished with 276 total yards on Saturday, converting just three of 10 opportunities on third down while committing three turnovers.

Although Western Michigan fell to 0-1, the future is bright as the team looks to capture a second straight MAC championship.

Juventus and AC Milan are set to face off at the Allianz Stadium this Sunday, with both sides hoping to keep their perfect winning records intact as the new season gets underway.

Currently sitting in fifth place in Serie A, Juventus have won both of their opening matches. Manager Luciano Spalletti's team began their campaign with a careful and controlled 1-0 win on the road against Frosinone. They then built on that momentum with an impressive 2-0 victory at home versus Parma, finding the net through Nico González and Teun Koopmeiners. The fact that they've kept clean sheets in both games shows just how solid their defence has been, even though they're dealing with plenty of injury problems across the squad.

Juventus are walking into this big match with a major injury headache. Spalletti is without seven important players, leaving the Bianconeri badly short on options, especially in attack and out wide.

The biggest blow came when it was confirmed that standout winger Kenan Yıldiz will miss around three months of action after breaking a bone in his foot.

To make matters worse, midfielder Khéphren Thuram is also out for several months with a serious issue and hasn't even been included in the club's official 25-man Serie A squad list.

Defender Juan Cabal and promising young forward Jeff Ekhator remain sidelined with long-term problems as well.

On top of all that, fullback Andrea Cambiaso picked up an ankle sprain in the Parma game and won't be available, while Weston McKennie has been training away from the main group.

Newly signed midfielder Pape Matar Sarr, who arrived on deadline day, is also ruled out because of a muscle injury, meaning Spalletti will need to tweak his tactical plans.

articles.body:
Barcelona will meet Valencia in their next La Liga encounter on Sunday as they look to continue their winning run in the new season.

Valencia vs Barcelona – Match preview and team news

Valencia CF faces a severe squad selection crisis ahead of their home clash at Mestalla against league leaders Barcelona. Manager Carlos Corberán is dealing with a heavily depleted roster, with six key first-team players officially ruled out due to injury.

The defensive unit is particularly stretched as José Copete recovers from meniscus surgery and Justin de Haas remains sidelined with a serious ankle problem.

In midfield and attack, Umar Sadiq's hamstring issue, alongside severe knee and ACL injuries to Sergi Canós and Diego López, deprives the team of critical tactical options.

At the same time, Guido Rodríguez remains out with a muscle tear. Furthermore, late fitness tests are required for Dimitri Foulquier, Luis Rioja, and backup goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen.

If they fail to clear medical checks, Valencia will be forced to rely on a highly experimental 5-3-2 setup anchored by Stole Dimitrievski in goal.

FC Barcelona heads into Mestalla in high spirits with major squad reinforcements ready for Hansi Flick's side.

The Blaugrana received a massive administrative boost as marquee summer signings Gabriel Jesus and goalkeeper Dominik Livaković were successfully registered and named in the travelling squad.

In midfield, the long-awaited return of Gavi provides a boost. The team received a brief scare when star winger Lamine Yamal missed full group training due to a minor knock, but Flick confirmed the teenager is fully fit and expected to start.

Long-term absentees Frenkie de Jong and Roony Bardghji remain unavailable due to knee injuries, alongside academy prospect Jesse Bisiwu.

Nevertheless, Barcelona boasts excellent squad depth, with Joan Garcia likely starting in goal and Raphinha spearheading the attack alongside Yamal and Fermín López.

Valencia CF has endured a miserable start to their new domestic campaign, managing just a single point from their opening three league fixtures. After showing brief defensive resilience in an opening 0-0 stalemate against RC Celta de Vigo, Los Che slumped to consecutive defeats. A narrow 1-0 home loss to Real Betis Balompié was followed by a disastrous 3-1 away defeat against RC Deportivo de La Coruña, leaving Carlos Corberán's side desperate for a tactical reset. 1

FC Barcelona has enjoyed a perfect start to their league journey under Hansi Flick, maintaining a 100% winning record after three matchdays. The Blaugrana opened their campaign with an emphatic 5-0 away triumph at Elche CF, before securing a mature 2-0 home victory against Athletic Club. They maintained their scoring touch last week by overpowering Rayo Vallecano 5-2 at home, confirming their status as early title favourites.

Barcelona: J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Espart; Pedri, Bernal; Yamal, Fermin, Gordon; Raphinha

articles.title: Everything Bryce Underwood Said About Michigan's Hail Mary in Controversial Win vs. Western Michigan
articles.summary: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood discussed the Wolverines' 13-12 victory over Western Michigan that contained a controversial Hail Mary finish on Saturday.
articles.body:
Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood discussed the Wolverines' 13-12 victory over Western Michigan that contained a controversial Hail Mary finish on Saturday.

"The thought was give my guys an opportunity, and that's what I did," Underwood told reporters after the game. "Excitement, we built a lot of trust over the last eight or nine months. So, I gave him an opportunity and he made the play."

Underwood also revealed that Michigan practiced Hail Marys several times in the week leading up to the game.

With seven seconds left in the fourth quarter, the Wolverines trailed 12-7 and had the ball at Western Michigan's 47-yard line. A Hail Mary attempt by Underwood went past the back of the end zone as time ran out, although officials reviewed the play and put one second on the clock.

On Michigan's second Hail Mary, JJ Buchanan hauled in a deep pass from Underwood for the game-winning touchdown.

"I don't know what I saw," Buchanan said after the game, per On3.com's Clayton Safie . "I just saw the ball, and I attacked it."

"The team needed a play, and there's not too much practice that goes into that, you just run down and see the ball," he added. "When I caught it, it was just relief."
